title: Cardinal Wright and the Pittsburgh jazz festival
summary: Bishop Wright arranged festivals in Pittsburgh with Father Woods's help; she left them to George Wein.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Tell me about Cardinal Wright in Pittsburgh.

Yes, that is something else. Father Woods got in touch with him. See, I went to Pittsburgh, I was back and forth to Pittsburgh for two years. Father called me one day and said, "Why don't you come back to New York to play your music. I'll tell you what to do. Get in touch with (he was a Bishop then) Bishop Wright." He wired Bishop Wright; A friend of mine, A.W. Stubble, wired him.

And so Father Woods had gotten in touch with me to help me. He saw me right away. So I had never been in front of a Bishop and I felt so strange. I just looked at him, you know, with all these colors on and everything. He said, "What can I do for you?" I said, "Jazz, jazz. There won't be any jazz after while." He looked at me and I told him about mother. He had confirmed them and all these people and he loved her, because he has - he does many, many favors for black people. He cleaned up Wiley Avenue where the dope addicts and all that was and he just does a lot of favors. I understood that he gave a man $12,000 for a project and the Ku Klux burned a cross on him before he went to Europe because he did that, you know, it was publicized. So he threw up his hands and he said, "We'll put on a festival for you." He must have gotten somebody least to put up at 50 to 75 thousand dollars because the musicians cast tossed $25,000 dollars to go in. So they did this festival every year. I got out of it because I got hold of George Weir to do it and I didn't think I should go down as a producer of a thing like that. I just let him take it all over himself, you know. I did two or three of the concerts, then I got out of it because I didn't want to wear myself out in Pittsburgh.
It was a pretty tough town. The reason I went
was because that is not an artistic town. Sometimes you can be lucky enough to start something up that's never happened in an old rusty broken-down town like that.
What's happened with the festival? Are they still going on with it?
... They failed in it so they got George Wein (Wing?) back over there again. The Gulf Oil was sponsoring one cat over there and it wasn't too good.
